result.title: LIFT: Latent Flow Matching for Probabilistic Cell Fate Dynamics with Single Cell Snapshots
result.summary: Lineage tracing links cell states through clonal ancestry, but does not generally identify unique source-descendant pairings. Learning from such data therefore requires a model of conditional outcomes, rather than only the terminal population distribution. We introduce LIFT, a latent flow framework for probabilistic cell-state generation from lineage-informed couplings. Variational inference encodes alternative outcomes in a latent space, while a conditional prior enables sampling from the initial state alone. A Mean Flow decoder predicts future cell state directly, requiring one decoder evaluation per sampling, which makes it convenient to predict cell fate through large scale Monte-Carlo sampling. This construction combines a representation of one-to-many relationships with efficient sampling and an analysis of conditional prediction error. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets demonstrate LIFT's ability to recover both population distribution and cell fate probabilities.

AI.brief_summary: LIFT 用变分推断把单细胞谱系追踪中的一对多命运结果编码到 latent 空间，配合条件先验实现仅凭初始状态采样，并用 Mean Flow 解码器一次评估直接预测未来细胞状态。论文在合成与真实数据上验证其能同时恢复群体分布与细胞命运概率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其 latent 空间 + 条件先验 + 单步解码器的 flow matching 构造，可能为 LVR 中「由初始证据状态采样生成 latent 推理状态」及少步/并行状态更新的设计提供可核查线索，但领域为计算生物学，与视觉多模态推理无直接关联。
